chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about fasting in Mecca and Medina while we were traveling. He said: 'It is obligatory (fard).' I said: 'No, but it is voluntary (ta-taww'u), just as prayer is performed voluntarily.' He said: 'You say: today and tomorrow.' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do not fast.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting while traveling in Mecca and Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) addresses the specific ruling of fasting while traveling in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Although the Imam initially affirms that fasting there is a 'fard' (obligatory duty), he clarifies that for the traveler, it functions as voluntary worship (tatawwu'), similar to extra prayers. Consequently, he instructs the traveler not to fast, emphasizing the ease and exemption granted to travelers even within the sanctified precincts.
